m:grandplace: The square is free and always open. The Town Hall can be visited with an audio guide (€15): Monday, Wednesday and Sunday 11am–5pm (last entry 4pm), Friday and Saturday 3–7pm (last entry 6pm), closed Tuesday and Thursday. At weekends there's also a guided tour with a climb up the tower (€25). No cash payments; tickets online or at the reception under the tower (bruxelles.be). Hours and price of the Maison du Roi: to be checked. Restaurants on the square cost more (one online guide says 30–50% more): eat two streets away. Watch out for pickpockets.
m:galeries: Entry is free, every day. Each shop has its own hours (usually open from morning to evening, to be checked); in the evening the gallery stays lit. For a historic break there's Mokafé (see «Where to eat»).
m:manneken: The statue is outdoors and free to see, always. The city schedules 23 «dressings» on fixed dates each year (calendar on the city website). The GardeRobe (Rue du Chêne 19) is open Tuesday to Sunday 10am–5pm; closed on Mondays and on 1 January, 1 May, 17 June, 1 and 11 November, 25 December. Ticket €5 (€10 with the City Museum at the Maison du Roi); free for under-18s and on the first Sunday of every month. Best to book online (mannekenpis.brussels).
m:stgery: Free to walk around. It's an area of bars and restaurants, good for a break or for dinner (see «Where to eat»). Keep bags and phone in front of you, especially in the evening.
m:cathedrale: Entry is free. Open Monday–Friday 8am–6pm, Saturday 8am–5pm, Sunday 1–6pm; no entry during services (Sunday masses at 9:30 and 11am). Paid: the Treasury €3 and the Romanesque remains €2, cash only; the crypt (€4) by booking only. The tower climb (€15, about two and a half hours, March to October) is reserved for groups booked weeks ahead. Source: cathedralisbruxellensis.be.
m:bd: Hours and price come from online guides, not the official website (comicscenter.net, to be checked): open Tuesday to Sunday 10am–6pm, closed Mondays; ticket €14.
m:montdesarts: Free to walk around. The Royal Palace can usually only be visited at certain times of year (not checked: see palaisroyal.be). The Musical Instruments Museum (MIM) is in the Art Nouveau building on the Mont des Arts: hours and price (€15–18 according to different guides) to be checked.
m:musees: Open Tuesday–Friday 10am–5pm and Saturday–Sunday 11am–6pm; closed on Mondays and on 1 January, 1 May, 1 and 11 November, 25 December; on 24 and 31 December they close at 3pm. Ticket desks close at 4:30pm on weekdays and 5:30pm at weekends. Magritte ticket €13, Oldmasters €13, combined €20; ages 18–25 €5; under 18 free; valid for one day. Every first Wednesday of the month from 1pm entry is free (4 November and 2 December 2026), with a free ticket at the desk. With an online ticket you enter from Place Royale 2, without a ticket from the desk at Rue de la Régence 3. The Wiertz Museum in Ixelles is closed for works. Source: musee-magritte-museum.be and fine-arts-museum.be.
m:sablon: Free to walk around. Flea market on Place du Jeu de Balle (usually every morning) and Sablon antiques (usually at weekends): hours not checked, see visit.brussels. From the Marolles to Place Poelaert there's a free public lift (hours to be checked). The Palace of Justice has had scaffolding outside for many years: admire it from outside.
m:atomium: Open every day 10am–6pm, last entry 5:30pm. On 24 and 31 December 10am–4pm (last entry 3:30pm); on 25 December and 1 January noon–6pm. Closed from 18 January to 5 February 2027 for annual maintenance. Adult ticket (18–64) €17, with five spheres and the Design Museum; buying online adds a booking fee (amount not stated). The Design Museum is open 11am–7pm. Take metro 6 to Heysel, then five minutes on foot. Source: atomium.be.
m:cinquantenaire: The park is free and always open. Hours and prices for the nearby museums come from online guides, not the official websites (to be checked): the Art & History Museum Tuesday–Friday 9:30am–5pm and Saturday–Sunday 10am–5pm, €10; Autoworld €15–18 (guides disagree); Parlamentarium free (hours on europarl.europa.eu). Some museum rooms may be closed for works.
vd:mokafe: A historic café inside the Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert: have a coffee or a waffle seated under the gallery's glass roof, or standing at the counter.
vp:mokafe: A coffee with a waffle usually costs €7–10 (menu not seen). Hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
vd:fritland: A frites shop near the Bourse: a cone of crispy double-fried chips, finished with the sauce you like (mayonnaise, andalouse and many more). Eaten standing up or as you walk.
vp:fritland: A cone usually costs €3.50–5.50 (an online guide gives €2–4 for friteries in general; menu not seen). Hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
vd:fin: A tavern serving Belgian home cooking in the lanes near Sainte-Catherine, with close wooden tables and dishes like stoemp (mash with vegetables), carbonnade and meatballs. Usually no bookings and you may have to wait.
vp:fin: A main course is around €14–18 (menu not seen); usually paid in cash (to be checked). Hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
vd:roue: A historic brasserie a short walk from the Grand-Place, with walls painted in tribute to the Belgian surrealist painters: classic Belgian cooking like moules-frites and carbonnade.
vp:roue: A main course usually costs €20–28 (menu not seen). Hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
vd:mort: The historic 1928 café near the Galeries, specialising in Belgian beers (gueuze, kriek, lambic): dark wood rooms and mirrors, and simple dishes like croque-monsieur and cheeses.
vp:mort: A beer is around €3–5 and a croque-monsieur about €8–12 (menu not seen). Hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
vd:cirio: A historic café opposite the Bourse, with an Art Nouveau room and mirrors: here you drink «half en half», white wine and sparkling wine in equal parts, with a sandwich or a cold dish.
vp:cirio: A glass and a sandwich are around €10–14 (menu not seen). Hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
vd:wittamer: A historic pâtisserie and chocolate shop on Place du Grand Sablon, with a tea room: cakes, pralines and an elegant break. A box of chocolates is the classic Brussels souvenir.
vp:wittamer: A pastry with a coffee is around €9–13 (menu not seen). It may be closed on Mondays: hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
vd:vieux: A brasserie on the Sablon square with classic Belgian dishes: moules-frites, carbonnade, croquettes. Prices for an upmarket area: the indoor room is better than a table on the square.
vp:vieux: A main course is around €18–26 (menu not seen). Hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
vd:stekerl: A Marolles bistro with Belgian and French home cooking, on a quiet street in the working-class district: meat dishes, close tables and a local crowd.
vp:stekerl: A main course is around €18–25 (menu not seen). Book ahead; closed on Sundays and Mondays according to my information, to be confirmed.
vd:antoine: The most famous frites stand in the European quarter, on Place Jourdan: the queue is long at peak times, but cones of chips with lots of sauces are a Belgian classic to eat standing up.
vp:antoine: A cone usually costs €3.50–6 (menu not seen). Hours are a cautious estimate, to be confirmed.
cd:mim: Seven thousand instruments in an Art Nouveau building, with headphones that play as you approach.
cd:chocostory: The story of Belgian chocolate with live demonstrations and tastings.
cd:autoworld: Six hundred vintage cars in the Cinquantenaire pavilion.
cd:horta: The house and studio of Victor Horta, the master of Brussels Art Nouveau.
cd:minieurope: Europe's monuments in miniature, at the foot of the Atomium.
cd:belvue: The history of Belgium since 1830, in a palace near the Royal Park.
cd:scienzenat: Dinosaurs and the world's largest iguanodon skeleton.
cd:citymuseum: On the Grand-Place: the collection of Manneken-Pis costumes and the history of Brussels.
